title: Local coordinates for a closed immersion of smooth schemes
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X\to S$ and $Y\to S$ be smooth morphisms [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and let $i:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion over $S$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For every $y\in Y$ there are integers $a,b\geq0$, an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq X$ of $i(y)$ [def-weil-open-immersion], and an etale $S$-morphism $h:U\to\mathbf A^{a+b}_S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space], such that $V=Y\times_XU$ is the scheme-theoretic inverse image of the coordinate subspace $\mathbf A^a_S\subseteq\mathbf A^{a+b}_S$ given by the last $b$ coordinates equal to zero, and $V\to\mathbf A^a_S$ is etale [def-pc-base-change]. The ideal sheaf of $V$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf] is generated by the pullbacks of those last $b$ coordinate functions, which form a regular sequence (each is a nonzerodivisor modulo its predecessors).

source.place: Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure; regular-sequence assertion in its proof, using divisors.tex Tag 067U, lemma-immersion-smooth-into-smooth-regular-immersion.

proof.text: Restrict the base to an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ containing the image $s$ of $y$. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-regular-immersion] to the restricted smooth closed pair. Obtain an affine neighbourhood $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $i(y)$ and an $A$-regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_b$ whose quotient $B=A/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ defines $Y_0=Y\times_XX_0$. The affine smoothness comparison [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] identifies $R\to A$ and $R\to B$ as smooth ring maps. In particular both are finitely presented, by [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map], and flat by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat].

source.place: Tag 0FUE, first paragraph, using divisors.tex Tag 067U; morphisms.tex Tag 01V6 and smooth flatness

proof.text: Apply [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form] to $Y_0\to W$ at $y$. It supplies an affine base neighbourhood $W'$, an open neighbourhood $Y_1$ of $y$, and an étale map $Y_1\to\mathbf A^a_{W'}$. The topology of a closed subscheme is the subspace topology, so choose an ambient open $O\subset X_0$ with $O\cap Y_0=Y_1$. Choose a principal affine neighbourhood of $i(y)$ inside $O\cap X_{W'}$, and replace $X_0$ by it and $W$ by $W'$. The restricted $Y_0$ is affine and lies in $Y_1$. Its map $\bar h:Y_0\to\mathbf A^a_W$ is still étale: restriction is composition with an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. Regularity of the $f_j$ survives this localization: an element killed after localization is killed by a power of the denominator beforehand, and injectivity in each successive quotient forces it to vanish after localization. The final quotient remains nonzero since it has the point $y$. The new $X_0$ and $Y_0$ are open in $X\times_SW$ and $Y\times_SW$ for the new $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$, and smoothness passes to open subschemes (a lifting from a first-order thickening of affine schemes lands in the open, the two having the same underlying space); so, as in step 1, [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] makes the new $R\to A$ and $R\to B$ smooth, hence finitely presented [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map] and flat [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-flat]. Write $\bar g_j\in B$ for the coordinates of $\bar h$, and lift them to $g_j\in A$ using the quotient surjection $A\to B$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, choice and lifting of the etale coordinates; morphisms.tex Tag 054L

proof.text: Set $P=R[t_1,\ldots,t_{a+b}]$ and let $P\to A$ send $t_j$ to $g_j$ for $j\leq a$ and $t_{a+j}$ to $f_j$. This defines $h:X_0\to\mathbf A^{a+b}_W$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. This map is finitely presented: write $A=R[z_1,\ldots,z_N]/(F_1,\ldots,F_c)$, choose polynomial representatives $G_j$ for the $g_j$ and $H_j$ for the $f_j$, and use the presentation $A=P[z_1,\ldots,z_N]/(F_i,t_j-G_j,t_{a+j}-H_j)$. The inverse of this presentation sends each $z_i$ to its original class and each $t_j$ to its prescribed image; the two composites fix all generators. Also $A\otimes_P P/(t_{a+1},\ldots,t_{a+b})=A/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)=B$: the forward map sends $u\otimes\bar p$ to $u\,p(g,f)\bmod(f)$ and its inverse sends $\bar u$ to $u\otimes1$. Thus the coordinate-subspace square is Cartesian before any étaleness assertion about $h$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, displayed coordinate map and finite-presentation permanence; explicit finite presentation and fibre-product computation

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(s)$, write $z=h(y)\in\mathbf A^{a+b}_k$ and let $w\in\mathbf A^a_k$ be the same point on the coordinate subspace. Set $L=\mathcal O_{(X_0)_s,y}$, $T=\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^{a+b}_k,z}$, $Q=\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^a_k,w}$ and $D=\mathcal O_{(Y_0)_s,y}$. The ring $L$ is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-fibre-regular-local]. The ring $T$ is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-smooth] and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-over-field-regular-local]. They are Noetherian, and $L$ is Cohen--Macaulay: a minimal system of generators of its maximal ideal has length $\dim L$ and is regular by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence]. Apply [lem-pur-relative-regular-equations-base-change] to $R\to A$, its flat quotient $B$, and $R\to k$. The prime for $y$ contains all the $f_j$; consequently the specified $f_j$ form a regular sequence in $L$, and $D=L/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)L$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, local rings on the fibre; divisors.tex Tag 0FUD, algebra.tex Tags 00TT and 00NQ

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] successively in $L,L/(f_1),\ldots,L/(f_1,\ldots,f_{b-1})$. These are Noetherian local rings, and each next equation is a nonzerodivisor in the maximal ideal, so $\dim L=b+\dim D$. In $T$ the last $b$ variables also form a regular sequence: after killing predecessors the polynomial quotient is a polynomial ring in the remaining variables, where multiplication by the next variable shifts coefficients injectively; localization preserves that injection. Its final local quotient is $Q$. Applying the same dimension-drop lemma gives $\dim T=b+\dim Q$. Base change preserves the étaleness of $\bar h$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]; the affine ring comparison [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] and [lem-sc-etale-local-dimension] therefore give $\dim D=\dim Q$. Hence $\dim L=\dim T$, including $b=0$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, dimension comparison; more-algebra.tex Tag 07QP; algebra.tex Tag 00KW

proof.text: The local fibre ring $L/\mathfrak m_TL$ equals $D/\mathfrak m_QD$: the last variables belong to $\mathfrak m_T$, their images are the $f_j$, and $T/(t_{a+1},\ldots,t_{a+b})=Q$. This is the local ring at $y$ of a fibre of the étale morphism $\bar h_s$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points] it is a finite separable field extension of $\kappa(z)=\kappa(w)$, hence has dimension zero. All three hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-miracle-flatness] now hold for the local map $T\to L$: $T$ is regular, $L$ is Cohen--Macaulay, and $\dim L=\dim T+0$. Therefore $T\to L$ is flat.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, finite local fibre and miracle flatness; algebra.tex Tag 00R4; morphisms.tex Tag 02GL

proof.text: Let $R_0=\mathcal O_{W,s}$, $T_0=\mathcal O_{\mathbf A^{a+b}_W,h(y)}$ and $L_0=\mathcal O_{X_0,y}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre] to $R_0\to T_0\to L_0$ and $M=L_0$. Both algebras are essentially finitely presented over $R_0$: they are prime localizations of the finite-presentation algebras $R_0[t_1,\ldots,t_{a+b}]$ and $A\otimes_RR_0$, respectively (tensor the presentation of $A$ in step 3). The module $M$ is free of rank one over $L_0$ and nonzero. It is flat over $R_0$ by [lem-pc-smooth-flat]. Its reduction modulo the maximal ideal of $R_0$ is the flat $T$-module $L$ from step 6; the quotients are precisely the displayed fibre local rings, since localization and quotient send $u/v$ to its residue fraction. The criterion gives flatness of $T_0\to L_0$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, fibre criterion; Tag 039C, theorem-criterion-flatness-fibre, algebraic input Tag 00R7

proof.text: Put $N=(\Omega_{A/P})_y$. It is a finite $L_0$-module: the finite presentation in step 3 makes the differentials of its finitely many algebra generators generate $\Omega_{A/P}$ by additivity and the Leibniz rule [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Differential base change [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], followed by localization, identifies $N/\mathfrak m_{T_0}N$ with the differentials over $\kappa(h(y))$ of the local fibre ring. Localization of differentials follows directly from their universal property: a derivation extends uniquely by $\mathrm d(u/v)=v^{-1}\mathrm du-uv^{-2}\mathrm dv$. The fibre of $h$ at $h(y)$ equals the fibre of $\bar h$ at the corresponding point of the coordinate subspace, by step 3. Since $\bar h$ is étale, that fibre is étale over $\kappa(h(y))$ [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. It is affine, the spectrum of $B\otimes_{R[t_1,\ldots,t_a]}\kappa(h(y))$, so the affine ring comparison [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine] makes its module of differentials over $\kappa(h(y))$ zero, and hence also its localization at $y$. Thus $N/\mathfrak m_{L_0}N=0$. Nakayama [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], with the empty generating family, yields $N=0$. The finite presentation in step 3, flatness in step 7 and [lem-sc-etale-at-prime-flat-unramified-criterion] now give a principal open $U\subseteq X_0$ containing $i(y)$ on which $h$ is étale.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, application of morphisms.tex Tag 02GU; algebra.tex Tags 00RV, 00DV and 00U6 spell out the pointwise criterion

proof.text: For $V=Y\times_XU$, step 3 gives $V=U\times_{\mathbf A^{a+b}_W}\mathbf A^a_W$ scheme-theoretically. Its map to $\mathbf A^a_W$ is étale by base change [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change]. The ideal is generated by the pullbacks of the last $b$ coordinates, which are exactly the restrictions of $f_1,\ldots,f_b$; localization preserves their successive multiplication injections by the fraction argument of step 2. Finally $\mathbf A^n_W\to\mathbf A^n_S$ is an open immersion: over each affine base chart it is restriction to the inverse image of the open $W$, by [def-sbc-affine-space]. Composition with this inclusion preserves étaleness [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. The zero-coordinate inverse image is still $V$, since $U$ lies over $W$. These are all the required assertions over the original base $S$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, conclusion and coordinate-subspace square; morphisms.tex Tags 02GO, 02GP and 02GN
